segments: Tenth Dynasty.
The Arab Kings.
the river called Khālam,
Anushtakin the eunuch attacked Mas'ud, along with a thousand other slaves.
And they bound him and brought him before his blind brother,
the one whom they had wished to make king over them.
Now his brother said to him:
"I will not do to you as you did to me,
but choose for yourself a place to which you may be sent,
and with you whomever you choose from your family."
So he asked to be sent to the fortress called Kassa (Kīrī?);
and he was conveyed thither with great honor and care.
Then the nobles took counsel,
and by deceit took the signet ring from Muhammad,
and sent it with some men to the governor of that fortress.
And they opened to them,
and they entered and killed Sultan Mas'ud.
Now Mawdud, the son of Mas'ud,
who was in Khwarazm,
when he heard what had happened {OCR?} to his father,
gathered five thousand [men],
and marched against the twenty thousand who were with his uncle,
and defeated them,
and killed his uncle.
And he bored through the ankles of the murderers of his father,
bound them with ropes,
and dragged them on the ground until they perished.
And he returned to Ghazna,
and the kingdom of his father was established for him,
except for Khorasan and Azerbaijan,
for the Turks ruled over them (over these).
And in the year 1353
[1353] of the Greeks,
(1042 of our Lord?),
which is the year 433
[433] of the Arabs,
Michael, king of the Romans, died without children.
And his two daughters, Zoe and Theodora, directed the kingdom for three months.
And then the nobles of the Romans took counsel,
and chose from among themselves (their sons) three individuals who were worthy of kingship.
And they wrote their names on pieces of paper,
and placed them inside wax pellets.
And they brought a little boy,
and he put forth his hand and drew out one of them;
and the name of Monomachos came out.
And they gave him Theodora, daughter of King Michael, as wife,
and made him king,
and called his name Constantine.
And that Theodora gave to Zoe, her sister, nine talents of gold in exchange for the kingdom.
Now this Constantine was magnanimous and lavish in gifts,
but he had the disease of podagra (gout).
